name: Fornax Dwarf
tagline: A Milky Way satellite spheroid 455,000 light-years out — the only classical dwarf still forming stars until recently.
history: Fornax is the most luminous of the Milky Way's classical dwarf spheroidals and the only one that kept making stars almost to the present day — a clue that it fell into the halo relatively recently. It owns six globular clusters of its own, including one of the oldest known. Its clumpy star-formation history makes it a laboratory for how dwarf galaxies evolve under a giant host's tides.
